item: GET /api/database/backup refuses a request from another site, writes its snapshot beside the database and takes one at a time
summary: The route wrote a full plaintext snapshot of the corpus into the operating system's temporary directory for any GET, so a page of another site could make the machine copy its corpus with one img tag. The refusal now lives in the route (not the middleware, R214): the Host must be a name the DNS-rebinding guard serves (a page on a name rebound to 127.0.0.1 is same-origin with itself and could read the answer), Sec-Fetch-Site must be same-origin or none, and Origin (else Referer) must name the request's own Host, all of them having to pass; a caller that sends none of the three (curl, a script) is served. STATED LIMIT, two forms: a browser without Fetch Metadata (Firefox before 90, Safari before 16.4, an old webview), and any browser asked for an OO_ALLOWED_HOSTS name over plain HTTP (browsers attach Fetch Metadata only to loopback and HTTPS targets), sends none of them for an img with referrerpolicy no-referrer, so it is served: the page cannot read the answer, the machine writes the snapshot, and the slot and the space gate bound the cost. The snapshot goes in a .oo-backup-* folder (mode 0700) beside the database; a free-space gate compares the database plus its WAL with the volume (507 with both figures: 'up to' the sum, a conservative upper bound, or 'at least' when a size could not be read; an unreadable volume or file size is not a refusal and the response carries X-OO-Free-Space-Check: not-read); one snapshot is made at a time per process (429; two servers on one data folder can each make one, R176); a FileResponse subclass removes the folder and frees the claim in a worker thread, shielded from cancellation, when the response ends or fails; the claim carries a token so a download taken over after 24 h cannot free the takeover's claim; a sweep removes only .oo-backup-* folders older than 24 h (several servers per data folder stay safe, R176), and only this route runs it (the boot sweep of stream_backup and the forensics staging list do not know the prefix, so a snapshot that a graceful shutdown abandons mid-write waits for the next call too: 0.5.1 item 41; the response does not watch for a client that went away, so the file is read to its end and the claim held until then: 0.5.1 item 42). An encrypted store is still refused (400). GET is kept. 48 tests: eight foreign forms refused before anything is written, through the app and by the route function alone, five rebound Host names, Origin deciding over Referer, own-page and non-browser callers served, both forms of the limit, location and mode, cleanup on failure, a mid-body failure, a plain cancellation and a level-triggered cancel scope, removal off the event loop, 507 (the log counted, exact room served, the volume measured, 'at least'), unreadable sizes, a stop that is not an Exception, 429, stale takeover and token ownership, sweep.
